# Internet Archive Wayback Machine

> > The Internet Archive's Wayback Machine preserves over 866 billion web pages captured since 1996, providing historical snapshots of websites including those from Alexa Internet crawls.

The Wayback Machine is a digital archive of the World Wide Web maintained by the Internet Archive, a San Francisco-based nonprofit. It allows users to browse archived versions of web pages across time, preserving the history of the internet for researchers, historians, and the public.

## Key Topics

- Wayback Machine
- Internet Archive
- Alexa Internet crawls
- Web archiving
- Historical website snapshots

- Time-based browsing

## Notable Archived Corporate & Entertainment Sites

- [Disney.go.com (1999)](http://web.archive.org/19990423182314/disney.go.com/): Archived Disney homepage from April 1999 captured via Alexa Internet crawl, showcasing late-90s web design and Disney's early internet presence
- [David Lynch Official Site (2008)](https://web.archive.org/web/20080303234450/http://www.davidlynch.com/): Archived official website of filmmaker David Lynch from March 2008, preserving his unique digital presence
- [Spectra Animation (2009)](https://web.archive.org/web/20090206093601/http://spectra-animation.ca/): Archived homepage of Spectra Animation studio from February 2009, documenting the Canadian animation company's web presence

## Archived Social Networks & Community Sites

- [Multimania (2012)](https://web.archive.org/web/20121206132202/http://multimania.tv/): Archived Russian social network and video platform Multimania from December 2012, preserving a snapshot of Eastern European social media history
- [We Are Little Stars (2002)](https://web.archive.org/web/20020331023129/http://wearelittlestars.com/): Archived landing page from March 2002, capturing early 2000s web design and community site aesthetics
